_comment: Roadmap-estate ratchet (road-to-estate-drawdown T2 + T3). The estate does not walk down by itself: new roadmaps arrive faster than old ones terminate, and until this file existed nothing in CI objected — lint_roadmap_family_cap bounds concurrency WITHIN one road-to-<family>-* family, and no gate read the estate as a whole. The baseline below is the MEASURED estate at registration, not a target: a hard target gate would be red on the day it lands and would teach the reader to ignore it. It fails on GROWTH instead, so the number can only walk down. T1's proposed ceilings are recorded under `target` and are explicitly NOT registered — they are the maintainer's to set.

metric.basis: src/scripts/check_estate_count.ts, using collect() from update_roadmap_progress — the same parser the dashboard is generated from, imported rather than re-implemented
metric.active_roadmaps: non-draft roadmap candidates at the top level of agents/roadmaps/, as collect() counts them. Verified 2026-08-18: this is exactly the number the dashboard header prints as 'N open roadmaps'.
metric.later_roadmaps: roadmap-shaped *.md files under agents/roadmaps/later/ — the same is_roadmap_candidate name filter the active side uses, so later/README.md is not counted. Counted from the filesystem because parked roadmaps sit outside collect()'s corpus by design; they are estate all the same, and a drawdown that moved everything into later/ and called the number down would be the burial T1's quality anchor exists to prevent.
metric.open_blockers: open blockers summed over the active tree AND later/. This deliberately does NOT equal the dashboard header's blocker count, which is active-only: counting only the active tree meant PARKING a roadmap dropped this number without resolving anything, and the ratchet then printed 'free tightening' over a burial. AC-1 is phrased on this metric, so it has to survive a move that resolves nothing. archive/ and skipped/ stay out — those are terminal, and a blocker in a skipped roadmap is not open work.
not_gated: the needs-you subset of open blockers — it moves when a blocker changes OWNER, which is not estate growth, so gating it would red on a reclassification that changed nothing about the size of the estate
agents/roadmaps/skipped/ and archive/ — these are the terminal destinations a drawdown sends files to; gating their growth would penalise the wanted direction

agents/roadmaps/stubs/ as a COUNT — a stub is not yet a roadmap, so it is not estate. It IS recognised as an offset destination and as an addition source, because un-stubbing is the documented promotion path and T3 has to be able to charge it.

baseline_history.why: registered with the gate, at the measured estate. Note the roadmap's own § 0 quotes 37 active / 44 later / 38 blockers against a mid-August pin; the estate moved between that draft and this registration, which is the arrival rate T3 exists to bound rather than a correction to the roadmap.

Two metrics REDEFINED before the gate ever ran on a second commit, both on R2 findings against this same change, so these are re-measurements rather than raises. later_roadmaps 44 -> 43: the first count included later/README.md, which the active side's own name filter excludes — an off-by-one that made the baseline describe 43 roadmaps plus a README. open_blockers 49 -> 67: the first count spanned the active tree only, so PARKING a roadmap dropped the gated number without resolving anything and the ratchet printed 'free tightening' over a burial. It now spans active + later/ (49 + 18), which is why the number rose while the estate did not. The cost is stated rather than hidden: this metric no longer equals the dashboard header, and the first version claimed that parity as a virtue.

open_blockers 67 -> 69, and this is a correction of a baseline that never described the trunk rather than room made for new growth. 67 was measured at 554b032aa, the commit that registered this gate (PR #1420). PR #1418 merged AFTER it and carried road-to-per-turn-hook-economy from one open blocker to three — verified by counting that one file at both refs, 1 at 554b032aa and 3 at 851568b5c, which is the entire delta. #1418's own CI ran before the gate existed, so nothing objected at the time and the trunk arrived at 69 with the file still claiming 67. The consequence was not a loose ratchet but a permanently red one: the count half compares the live tree against this baseline irrespective of the diff, so EVERY subsequent PR failed on growth it had not caused, and the first to notice was an evidence-only PR that adds no blocker at all. Raising to the measured trunk value restores the property the gate is for — it fails on growth from here, and 69 is now the number that must walk down. The two blockers themselves are untouched and remain open work on road-to-per-turn-hook-economy; closing or parking someone else's blockers to buy the old number back would have been a terminal disposition of another session's work, which is exactly what this ratchet must never incentivise.

RAISED by 3, on top of the 67 -> 69 correction above rather than beside it. All three are road-to-per-turn-hook-economy Phase 2, and each records a finding that would otherwise rot: b-payload-read-parse-dominates (two independent measurements now say D-2's cost is the dispatcher's own read+parse of the payload, once per event, not the per-concern churn the roadmap blamed — so the phase's AC is refuted and the null is published), b-payload-mis-nested-readers (two concerns read tool payload keys off the envelope root; one is a security scanner that works only via a whole-envelope fallback, the other returns 0 on every dispatcher-path call today), and b-stop-async-split-prerequisites (step 5.3 deferred, carrying the five prerequisites its classification surfaced). A blocker that puts a maintainer decision in front of the maintainer is the estate growing in the direction this ratchet exists FOR, which is why the raise is taken rather than the findings being dropped into prose where nothing tracks them. My first version of this entry claimed two of five as unattributed drift; the trunk's correction identified the same two and named their cause, so that half is withdrawn rather than restated.

LOWERED by 1 on each gated metric, in the direction this ratchet exists for. road-to-stop-gate-honesty reached zero open steps and zero deferred items and was archived, which is a terminal disposition rather than a park; its `b-detector-demotion-bars` was resolved with the decision recorded at the entry, not moved elsewhere. Both numbers are therefore measurements of a smaller estate, not room bought by relocating work — later_roadmaps is unchanged at 43, which is the check that distinguishes the two. Walked down because the count gate reported both as free tightening and its unit test asserts the committed budget equals the live tree: a baseline left above a lower measurement is headroom a later change can spend without any gate objecting, which is the loose-ratchet failure the 67 -> 69 entry above records from the other direction.

RAISED by 1 on active_roadmaps and open_blockers, and the direction is stated plainly because this ratchet exists to make exactly this visible. Both come from one change that routes a MEASURED hook-latency regression to an owner: the blocker b-concern-load-taxes-every-slot on road-to-per-turn-hook-economy, and road-to-slot-scoped-concern-loading for the structural half. The trunk is red on the pre-registered latency gate — main measured pre_tool_use p50 176 ms against a derivation window of 111-148, a local A/B at the gate own n=50 reproduced +12.6 percent, and the same-run control was flat, so it is cost growth rather than runner spread. The estate grew because the defect had nowhere to live, not because scope was added. NOT offset deliberately: the only offset available here would be archiving an unrelated roadmap to buy room, which bundles an unreviewed disposition into a latency-gate PR. The roadmap carries estate_offset_exempt with that reason and its own Honest null, so it closes on a measurement in Phase 0 if module load turns out to be a minor share — which is the walk back down this raise is underwritten by. later_roadmaps unchanged at 43, the check that distinguishes a real addition from work relocated into later/.

WALKED BACK DOWN, reversing the raise recorded one entry above IN THE SAME PR. That raise was explicitly underwritten by the new roadmap own Honest null — close on the Phase 0 measurement if the premise does not hold — and the null fired on the first measurement it took: a bundle carrying only the 11 pre_tool_use concerns loads in 24 ms against the full 45-concern bundle at 23 ms, so slot-scoping the dispatcher would have bought minus one millisecond. The bundle is dominated by its shared dependency graph, not by per-concern code. road-to-slot-scoped-concern-loading is therefore archived with that result published rather than left open, and b-concern-load-taxes-every-slot is resolved because the real cause was found and fixed in the same change: dispatch_hook parsed the 61 kB YAML manifest on every dispatch (8 ms module load plus 12 ms parse) and now reads a precompiled 14.7 kB JSON sibling, taking pre_tool_use p50 from 103 ms to 81 ms. Both numbers are measurements of a smaller estate, not room bought by relocating work — later_roadmaps is unchanged at 43, which is the check that distinguishes the two.

RAISED by 2 active and 1 blocker ON TOP of the same-day lowering recorded directly above, for the two roadmaps the long-horizon branch installed from an inbox handover and then executed in the same PR. The arithmetic is stated because the first version of this entry got it wrong: it read 38 -> 40 and 72 -> 73 against the pre-merge trunk, and `origin/main` had meanwhile MEASURED 37 and 71 by archiving road-to-stop-gate-honesty and resolving its blocker. Carrying 40/73 through the merge would have silently pocketed that branch’s drawdown as headroom, which is the loose-ratchet failure the 67 -> 69 entry records from the other direction. 37 + 2 and 71 + 1 is the honest merged value. Both roadmaps carry an `estate_offset_exempt` line, so the one-in-one-out check passes on its own terms; what still fires is the raw COUNT half, which is diff-blind by design. The honest shape of the raise: road-to-council-api-fallback arrives at 16 of 17 steps done and would have ARCHIVED in this PR — that archive is the offset the check wanted. It does not archive, because Iron Law 3 refuses a silent archive while a `[~]` item is unresolved and that resolution belongs to the user, so this is a raise one user decision turns back into 38. road-to-long-horizon-execution stays open on an OBSERVATION of a live killed-and-resumed run: not work any change-set can contain, and not something to buy back by archiving an unrelated roadmap, which would move the number without moving the estate. The +1 blocker is `team-loop-benchmark-spend`, which puts a funded-or-published-null decision in front of the maintainer — the direction this ratchet exists FOR.

road-to-estate-drawdown Phase 2 triage batch 1 — the first batch of the sweep this ratchet was registered to make stick. RE-APPENDED a SECOND time, after a second merge of origin/main, and every number below is re-measured on the merged tree rather than carried over from either previous reading. The trunk moved twice under this branch: first PR #1429 (a raise to 38/43/72 then its own walk back down to 37/43/71), then the long-horizon branch installing two roadmaps (37 -> 39 active, 71 -> 72 blockers). Both of those entries stand above this one in trunk order; this entry states only what THIS branch does to the numbers they left. Six of the ten files in the batch took the verdict PARK-PROBEABLE and moved to later/ with a rewritten resume condition. active_roadmaps 39 -> 36 is WALKED DOWN, and the delta is three rather than six because three of the six carried `status: draft` and were never in collect()'s corpus to begin with — the same asymmetry that explains the blocker delta below. later_roadmaps 43 -> 49 is RAISED by all six, because every parked file is counted there whatever its status was. The raise is exactly the move this metric exists to make visible: parking is not closing, and a drawdown that moved everything into later/ and called the number down is the burial T1's quality anchor forbids. It is taken rather than avoided because all six are the later/ definition verbatim — open work that cannot proceed now, gated on an external trigger, not abandoned — and every one keeps its open-step count plus a resume condition a script or a named command can test. ONE of the six is decidable by resume_probe and reports `unmet` (domain-pack-extraction-when-triggered); the other five are recorded with a per-row reason in agents/decisions/estate-triage-dispositions.yml, because their conditions name an external fact, a content bar, or a host capability rather than a file's existence. It was two until the R2 round showed the second was decidable only through a field-split bypass, and removing that bypass took the count down — a probe that decides fewer notes honestly is worth more than one that decides more by an authoring trick. open_blockers 72 -> 73 is +1 with one cause, stated because it looks like drift and is not: road-to-product-bets carried `status: draft`, so collect() excluded it and its one blocker was invisible to this metric; parking it into later/ brought that blocker into the counted corpus. No blocker was opened, closed or moved — a draft's blocker became countable. Nothing in this batch was archived, so no closure needed a migration note; the two DECISION-SHEET verdicts route to the existing consolidated sheet and the two EXECUTE verdicts leave their files in the active tree.

The two Iron-Law-3 holdouts resolved on a converged AI-council verdict — anthropic + openai, 2 of 2 present, one round, 2026-08-19 — and both roadmaps archived. active_roadmaps 36 -> 34 is WALKED DOWN by exactly those two archivals; later_roadmaps 49 -> 50 is RAISED by one, the follow-up carrier the council required for the second of them. open_blockers is UNCHANGED at 73, which is the check that says nothing was bought by relocating an open decision: both archived files carried only resolved blockers, and the new carrier carries none. The two cases were not the same case, and the council said so on both. road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-d-top-band-model-economy's holdout was an acceptance CRITERION that is unsatisfiable as written and contradicted in that form by ADR-035; both seats returned archive-with-no-follow-up, because a contradictory criterion is a specification defect rather than future work and a roadmap spawned from it could never close. They split on the glyph and `[-]` won on the sharper argument, verified against the tree before adoption: `[x]` would assert 'no .md names a vendor model', and 160 .md files do. road-to-council-api-fallback's holdout was a real proposal gated on an operational trigger, so it moved to a carrier rather than being archived with it — later/road-to-council-api-quota-source-split.md, with the step migrated verbatim including its 'do not build ahead of that evidence' instruction. Both seats independently REFUSED that roadmap's claim about itself that its deferral 'does not gate archival': a roadmap does not get to exempt itself from a repository-wide preservation rule, or the gate becomes discretionary exactly where it is structural. The claim is left standing in the archived file rather than deleted, because the claim is the finding. The carrier's resume condition is an existence predicate over a named evidence file, which resume_probe decides — chosen over the other seat's `gh issue list` probe because the tree has a probe for one and not the other, and both seats named parked-roadmap clutter as the failure mode of a follow-up whose trigger nothing can observe.

WALKED DOWN by 1 active and 2 blockers: road-to-inbox-harvest-residuals reached a terminal state and archived. Its last two open items, R1 and R2, were both blocked on a call rather than on effort, and both are now `[-]` against named locks — one of the three terminal states that roadmap's own Exit clause allows. later_roadmaps is UNCHANGED at 50, which is the check that says this is a closure and not a park: nothing was relocated to buy the number. The two blockers resolved are the roadmap's own, each on the option the blocker itself recommended — deferred-finding-decision-reopen on (b), cancel R2 against the in-source decline; spent-inbox-artifacts-await-deletion on (c), keep-reason recorded, the branch that deletes nothing. Neither was closed to make room: the AI council was polled first on whether an agent may record a disposition against a blocker whose declared Owner is the maintainer, and both seats converged that observing a named trigger did NOT fire closes the loop while the reserved call is whether to REOPEN — which is exactly what was not done. R2's trigger was probed rather than assumed (`check_review_dispositions`: 17 archived records, all terminal, zero findings, which is the trigger's negation), and R1's cancellation had to be RE-GROUNDED because the lock the step cited says the opposite of what the step claimed: § 2.7 of plan-review-gates.md opens with 'never an edit ban on the live artefact', and that same file already carried the refutation of the broader reading in writing. The lock that does hold is narrower — § 2.7 freezes only the 16 superseded round-review records, and the contract declined a corpus-migration event for this class when it made its v1 fields optional. A cancellation resting on a lock the cited contract denies would have been a burial wearing a citation, which is the failure this ratchet's own history keeps recording from the count side.

WALKED DOWN by 1 blocker: worktree-claim-root-split resolved in the change that found it. The blocker recorded a measured defect — the roadmap claim and the stop-slot concern resolved different roots, so run-continuation was inert in every worktree session — and the claim now lives in the git common dir beside the session register. Active and later are unchanged and net zero by construction: road-to-long-horizon-execution archived and road-to-run-continuation-observation was created in the same change to carry its last deferred criterion, per the preservation test the same change added to roadmap-progress-sync. Walked here rather than banked because the gate reported the slack itself, and a baseline above the measurement is headroom a later change spends with nothing objecting.

RAISED by 1 blocker, and the raise is the alternative to a silent drop rather than room made for new growth. road-to-run-continuation-observation step 0.1 carries the parent criterion "a process-full contract run finishes a 3-phase roadmap with zero synchronous contacts, re-engaging across turns, and opens the PR". Its sibling step 0.0 closed on a real engagement observed 2026-08-19, and 0.1 did NOT: this roadmap has one phase, so the three-phase half cannot be read off that run however the rest of it went, and closing it there would be the attribution error the step's own text warns against. The choice was therefore between recording the gap as three-phase-contract-run, where the dashboard and this ratchet both see it, and leaving it as prose in a step nobody counts — which is the invisible-gate failure road-to-solution-minimalism recorded when its own halt lived in prose and the generated dashboard published zero blockers for a roadmap stopped for four days. Active and later are unchanged, which is the check that this is not a park wearing a tightening's clothes. The entry is class 3 rather than 0 on purpose and that bounds what the raise buys: an agent does the work, but choosing which roadmap gets worked next is the operator's, so no command produces a qualifying run and this number walks back down on the first three-phase autonomous roadmap anyone finishes from a worktree — as a side effect, with no dedicated effort.

An UN-PARK, which is the one estate move this gate had no shape for. active_roadmaps 33 -> 34 is RAISED and later_roadmaps 50 -> 49 is WALKED DOWN, by the same single file moving in the same commit: later/road-to-request-scoped-rule-load.md returns to the active tree. Net estate is zero, and the two numbers move in opposite directions for that reason rather than by coincidence. Read the raise together with the walk-down or it reads as growth, which it is not: no roadmap was created, no work was added, and open_blockers is UNCHANGED at 71 because open_blockers already spans active plus later/ and therefore cannot notice a move between them. That invariance is the check that this is a disposition change and not a park wearing a tightening's clothes, in the exact mirror of the test the 2026-08-19 batch-1 entry above applies in the parking direction. WHY THE FILE MOVES: its resume condition, restated 2026-08-08 and owned by the maintainer, was 'Resume when P2.1 of road-to-rule-delivery-integrity closes'. P2.1's own completion marker in the archived parent reads done 2026-08-08, the parent archived 2026-08-09 at 259039157, and git log over the parked file since 2026-08-08 returns ZERO commits. So the condition has been satisfied for eleven days with nothing acting on it and nothing recording a decision not to, while three consecutive /roadmap:next screens logged the FIRED probe as a by-product finding and each correctly declined the work behind it as maintainer-owned. Declining the work and leaving the file parked are different acts, and only the first was ever decided. THE RAISE IS NOT UNDERWRITTEN BY FUTURE WORK, which distinguishes it from every prior raise in this history: nothing is promised, and it does not walk back down on a measurement. It walks down when Phase 4 terminates in either direction, and Phase 4 stays council-parked by the 2026-07-07 verdict with its design locked and both steps still open. The file carries estate_offset_exempt so the one-in-one-out half passes on its own terms; what fires is the raw COUNT half, which is diff-blind by design and cannot see that the offset it wants is the later/ decrement recorded on the very same line. The alternative was archiving an unrelated roadmap to buy the number back, which moves the count without moving the estate and is what this ratchet's own history repeatedly refuses. Left unrecorded, the shape has a worse cost than one raise: an un-park would be permanently unrepresentable, later/ would be a one-way door, and burial would be the cheapest disposition available - which is precisely the failure the later_roadmaps metric was added to prevent.

WALKED DOWN by 1 active roadmap: road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-b-dispatch-safety archived, its last open step closed. Nothing was parked and nothing was created to absorb it, which is the check that this is a real termination rather than a burial wearing a tightening's clothes. The step it closed had been deferred on a premise that turned out to be false: the zero producer count it waited on was produced by an unchecked validator rather than by producers, so the condition could never have been met. Its deferred half was relocated intact into an EXISTING active roadmap (road-to-subagent-lifecycle-integrity, as its own phase) rather than into a new one, which is why the active count falls by one instead of staying flat - a follow-up roadmap would have made this a net zero and bought nothing. READ TOGETHER WITH THE ENTRY ABOVE, or the arithmetic does not reconcile: this walk-down was authored against 33 active / 50 later and merged onto a base where the un-park had already moved those to 34 / 49. The active number below is therefore 33, not 32, and the later number is 49, not 50 - the difference is the parallel session's file, not a correction to this closure. Restated at merge rather than left at its authoring values, because a history entry that records a measurement nobody can reproduce against the tree is the staleness this ratchet's own metric note refuses.

RE-MEASURED AT MERGE, not carried over from either side, because both sides moved. This branch adopts road-to-single-delivery (+1 active) and opens four blockers on it (+4); the trunk meanwhile WALKED DOWN by archiving road-to-inbox-harvest-2026-08-b-dispatch-safety. Taking this branch authored numbers through the merge would have silently pocketed that archival as headroom, which is the loose-ratchet failure two earlier entries in this file record from the other direction. So the trunk file was taken whole and these numbers are the measurement on the merged tree: 33 + 1 = 34 active, 49 later unchanged, 70 + 4 = 74 blockers. WHAT THE +4 BUYS, since it is the larger half: partition-requires-global-layer HALTED Phase 2 mid-implementation - the partition leaves the project layer with 16 rules and zero skills, so a checkout with no current global install would silently drop from 111 rules and 338 skills to 16 and 0, which is an under-governed session rather than a token cost. compact-survival-of-package-only-rules carries four rules that stop surviving /compact once their unscoped global twin is gone, three of them Iron-Law bearing. overlap-check-binding-surface exists because two gates in this area already report to nobody. host-skill-suppression-capability is a host probe whose negative answer closes it. Each carries enumerated options and a recommendation rather than a flag. later_roadmaps unchanged at 49 is the check that nothing was parked to pay for any of this.

WALKED DOWN by 1 blocker, net of two resolutions and one new finding, which is why the delta is -1 rather than -2. RESOLVED: overlap-check-binding-surface, on a CONVERGED AI council verdict (2/2) - preflight, with both seats requiring the binding be provably live, which it now is. And partition-requires-global-layer, resolved to option (c) not by a vote but by a MEASUREMENT that eliminated option (a): consistency.yml runs task generate-tools on a fresh checkout, so refusing without a global layer would break the pipeline - the exact counter-case one seat had named against its own choice. OPENED: warn-path-unreachable-without-version-marker, and it is a finding against work this same branch marked DONE. Phase 3 instrumented the scope guard WARN verdict with an overlap count; measured, that branch never executes, because installed_version_at returns unknown for ~/.claude (no package.json beside a host directory) so every real cross-scope install classifies as DRIFT. The instrumentation is live and unreachable, which reads as coverage in the diff. Recording it as a blocker rather than silently repairing it is the point: it falsifies part of a completed phase. active and later unchanged, which says nothing was created or parked to absorb any of this.

RESTORED to 74, and this entry records a WRONG WALK-DOWN rather than growth. The entry directly above walked open_blockers 74 -> 73 on the grounds that two blockers resolved and one opened. Two did resolve. But Phase 2 had halted a SECOND time in the same change - on an undecidable current-global-layer predicate - and that halt was written as PROSE in step 2.0 instead of as a blocker. So the number of open DECISIONS never fell, only the number of recorded ones did, and the ratchet was satisfied by not writing something down. R2 review caught it: after the flip, no open blocker blocked Phase 2, the dashboard stopped explaining the halt, and lint_roadmap_blockers decidability fields never applied to the live decision. partition-current-layer-undecidable now carries it with three enumerated options and a recommendation, and 74 is the measurement again. The lesson is the one this file keeps recording from the other direction: a walk-down is only honest if the work it claims to have removed is actually gone.

RE-MEASURED AT MERGE, not carried over from either side, because both sides moved -- the same reason the row above states, and the second time in one day that this file has had to say it. This branch parks road-to-run-continuation-observation to later/ (-1 active, +1 later); the base it merged had itself moved to 34/49/74. Carrying this branch's earlier 32/50/70 forward would have described neither tree. open_blockers: 74 is the base's number, untouched, and that it is untouched is the check that this is a park and not a burial: the metric spans active AND later/ precisely so parking cannot print a free tightening over a blocker nobody resolved, and three-phase-contract-run is still open and still counted. Parked because every open item is gated on an external trigger this estate cannot supply: step 0.1 needs a process-full run over a roadmap carrying execution.mode: autonomous with open steps in three or more phases, and measured 2026-08-19 exactly three active roadmaps carried that mode while neither of the other two had open steps in three phases. process-full terminated on this roadmap as blocked-preflight, which is the mechanism agreeing with the disposition. The number walks back the moment it is un-parked. The unreconciled -1 this branch's earlier row recorded (commit 7d5114dbd walked open_blockers 71 -> 70 with no history row) is left where it is: the base has since re-measured to 74, so that gap is now historical rather than live, and inventing a reconstruction here would be a second unmeasured row.

RE-MEASURED AT MERGE. Both sides had moved: this branch's rows above were measured against 34/49/74, and the base it merged had parked a roadmap to later/ (33/50). Carrying either side's number forward would have described neither tree, so the values here are read off the merged filesystem. open_blockers stays 74, and the reason it stays is CHECKED rather than assumed - a net zero is the shape a walk-down hides in, which is what the row two above records going wrong on this same branch. Verified against origin/main: 4 open before, 4 open after, and the SETS differ. Resolved: partition-requires-global-layer (option (c), on a measurement that eliminated (a)) and overlap-check-binding-surface (converged council verdict). Opened: warn-path-unreachable-without-version-marker (a finding against completed Phase 3 work) and partition-current-layer-undecidable (Phase 2's second halt, which R2 review caught being carried as prose). Two out, two in - not one error cancelling another.

RAISED by 2 later roadmaps and WALKED DOWN by 2 active ones, one transfer: road-to-carrier-layer-convergence and road-to-surface-consolidation are parked to later/. Total estate is unchanged at 83, and open_blockers is unchanged at 74 -- which is the check that this is a park and not a burial, since that metric spans active AND later/ precisely so parking cannot print a free tightening over a blocker nobody resolved. All three blockers involved (b-convergence-machine, repo-admin-and-usage, benchmark-spend) stay open and stay counted. Both roadmaps were parked because every open item is gated outside the roadmap, which is the repository's own active-vs-later test: carrier's two remaining steps are both in Phase 3 behind a Class 3 maintainer-machine measurement, and surface-consolidation's one remaining step is a utilization sweep gated on a window that elapses ~2026-08-26 AND on usage evidence accumulating over it. `/roadmap:process-full` terminates on both at blocked-preflight with zero runnable open steps, so leaving them active would make the estate advertise work the command is required to refuse. This empties the ACTIVE AUTONOMOUS estate to zero, intentionally and as of 2026-08-19. The consequence is recorded at the three-phase-contract-run blocker of later/road-to-run-continuation-observation rather than smoothed over: its criterion is now CURRENTLY unreachable from the estate, which is not the same as impossible, and it is not weakened to match. AI council 2026-08-19, 2/2 convergent (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default, two rounds, blind peer review), which also made a visible parked-work inventory the condition of the disposition -- the same change adds one to the generated dashboard.

RE-MEASURED AT THE SECOND MERGE of this branch, same reason as the row above and worth the repetition: both sides had moved again. This branch measured against 33/50/74; the base parked two further roadmaps to later/ (31/52). Values read off the merged filesystem, not carried from either side. open_blockers stays 74 for the second time in a row, and for the second time that is CHECKED rather than assumed - a net zero is the shape a walk-down hides in, which is what the row three above records going wrong on this same branch. Verified against origin/main at 7be25cf07: 4 open before, 4 open after, and the SETS differ. Out: partition-requires-global-layer, overlap-check-binding-surface. In: warn-path-unreachable-without-version-marker, partition-current-layer-undecidable. Two out, two in - not one error cancelling another. That the identical net-zero has now appeared twice across two independent merges is corroboration, not a reason to stop checking it.

Raised 31 -> 32 for road-to-hook-state-followups.md, which carries the items PR #1458 saw and deliberately did not fix: two consumers reading paths nothing writes, the API shape the two lock primitives need before they converge, and 11 local test reds across 6 files that CI never reports and nobody owned.
